scene noonsky
: So, how far away is this book store thingy?
: Wait...your signing is at a book store, right? Because I have a library book I’ve been holding onto for five years now and I get nervous any time I have to go inside one.
: They’re onto me. I know they are.
: Does...Futaba know about this?
: No. And she never will, so keep your mouth closed.
: Hmm...I believe the venue is about a quarter mile away. But if it’s alright with you, I’d like to make another quick detour for more coffee.
: You are literally holding a cup of coffee right now.
: That I am. And if my calculations are correct, which they always are, I’ll be finished with that coffee by the time we arrive at the next shop.
: You have an addiction and you need help.
: As do you and no one ever tries to rehabilitate you.
: That’s because Sensei’s addiction keeps a bunch of girls from going crazy and rubbing up against stuff. Yours just keeps you awake.
: Ew. To the girls part. Not the awake part.
: I’m a girl. You’re a girl. Nodoka’s probably a girl. Are you saying we’re all gross as well?
: I’m saying I don’t want to have a casual conversation about our teacher’s sex addiction. Are we getting coffee or not?
: We are. But I must first take another detour to rub up against stuff as Sensei’s sickness hasn’t spread to me yet and I’m beginning to get a little crazy.
: Beginning? You’re already batshit insane. Sensei, I don’t want to take another detour. Can you just, infect Nodoka really quick or something? Thanks.
: No thanks. I’m sure I could, but I’m afraid of what I’d catch from her.
: You’d catch nothing but a good time. Come to me, Father. Infect me with your desire. Make me sick.
: Pretty sure the only one getting sick here is me...
scene black

No one becomes infected, but Nodoka does manage to obtain another cup of liquid courage that she carries along with her to the venue (Which, luckily for Rin, is not a library but a very large bookstore.)
Upon entering, I’m shocked to see just how many people turned up. And, while I’d love to be able to tell you that many of them are just here to shop...that doesn’t seem like the case.

Nodoka is recognized immediately and pulled away from our group so that she can get set-up at a table on the second floor of the shop, leaving the rest of us to awkwardly look around for something to do.
Carefully and slowly, we make our way through the crowd and manage to scope out a small space of unoccupied standing room that we quickly claim as our own.
Thanks to my height, I’m able to see over the crowd, but the same can’t be said for Rin and Otoha who struggle to stare between the gaps in onlookers.
There’s something bothering me, though.
I can’t seem to go five seconds without someone looking at me and whispering to their friends or partner about something.
Rin and Otoha catch onto this well, but don’t appear to understand why either.
It makes me very uncomfortable.
I never fit in anywhere to begin with, but drowning in this sea of inaudible gossip is starting to drive me-
: Attention, please. Today’s Q&A panel is about to begin.
: Please keep all questions brief and do not interrupt one another while someone is speaking.
: We understand just how many of you are passionate about the first installment of this new series, but we urge you to remain calm and collected as Miss Nagahara speaks.
: Repeat offenders will be escorted out of the venue and banned from attending any future events both related to and unrelated to today’s author.
: With that said, on behalf of the Kumon-mi Literary Committee, I’d like to thank today's guest for appearing and urge all of you to provide a very warm welcome...to S.A. Nagahara!
scene nodokabooksign1
The crowd erupts into a fit of applause as Nodoka- or, excuse me, S.A. Nagahara takes her seat at a table stacked with copies of what I can only imagine is her latest book.
Her composure and refusal to stop the crowd from applauding signals to me that she’s done this before, and I’m surprised to see just how well-established she is for her age.
Though, if she’s going to lie about her name, I’m sure that most of the people in this crowd are unaware of how old she really is in the first place.
The applause slowly dies down and, as it does, Nodoka’s eyes open.
scene nodokabooksign2
: Wooooow...quite the turn-out we have today, isn’t it?
: I suppose trying something a little different was worth it after all.
: You flatter me. You really do.
scene nodokabooksign3
: Now, let’s see...
: Normally, this is the part where I’d give a brief synopsis of the book. Maybe a little background information about how it came to be or why it came to be, but...
: Frankly, I don’t see why that would be necessary given that you’re already here, aren’t you?
scene nodokabooksign4
: You would not be here if you didn’t already know what this book was about.
: You would not be here if you weren’t already curious about the characters or the story...or what will come next.
: And so, perhaps it would be in everyone’s best interests if we skipped right over the formalities and just opened the floor.
: What do you say?
The crowd erupts again and, while it’s certainly loud and obnoxious, it takes some of the focus off of me.
And I’m thankful for that.
: Go on. Raise your hands. You know how this works.
scene nodokabooksign5
The hands go up and the volume goes down.
Then, almost mechanically, Nodoka begins moving through the audience one by one.
: Hmm...you. In the shirt. What would you like to know?
: Well, first off, I’d like to thank you for deviating from your typical formula and branching out into something far surpassing what the typical reader would call “taboo.”
: Which is saying a lot for an author who hasn’t shied away from including sex scenes containing literal farm animals.
: We all know what really happens on farms. I’m not one to shy away from the truth. But what is the question?
: The question is...why a school?
: There are so many other books and media series focusing on schools and, up until now, you’ve always seemed to challenge standard conventions and cliches.
: Are you calling my latest work cliche?
: Not at all! I-
scene nodokabooksign6
: I’m kidding. There’s no need to get flustered. It’s a good question.
scene nodokabooksign7
: I suppose the easiest answer would be...that a school simply is the perfect setting to facilitate the type of story I wanted to tell and the themes I wanted to explore.
: Anyone could mimic Nabokov. There are more “Lolita” clones than one can count — and it was not my goal to follow the same steps that many before me have tripped over.
scene nodokabooksign8
: But when you want to create an entire well of debauchery — a haven for misdeeds even, there is no better place to look than where the innocent gather most.
scene nodokabooksign9
: Next question...You. In the other shirt.
: Th-Thank you! Huge fan! I’ve been following you since “Every Day I Grow Some More!”
: Aww, you flatter me. What’s your question?
: M-My question is...how confident are you in ending a series with so many prospective love interests?!
: Up...Up until now, you’ve always cited “Why choose?” as a lazy, uninspired book trope! Have...Have you changed your opinion?!
: I have not. And, to be quite honest, I’m not too concerned with how the story will end at this point in time.
: What we have in “The Light of Last Summer” is not a run of the mill romance. In fact, I struggle to call it romance at all.
: It’s an in-depth character study of a large group of flawed and misguided individuals who, for the most part, do not deserve love.
: I’m sure you’d all agree that I am very good at what I do. But there is no conceivable way for any author to believably end a series with this many pairings in a way that is good for all of them.
: Some of the students will have to suffer for others to prosper. And in the prospering of those others, the sorrow in the background is sure to leak into everything else.
: No one can win, and I believe that is evident even this early on in the series.
: Is it just me or...does Nodoka’s new book sound a lot like...
: It’s not just you.
: That’s exactly what it is.
scene nodokabooksign10
: You. In the third shirt. Question?
: Yes! Hi! Uhh...let’s see...
: I actually have two questions.
: No you don’t. Pick one.
: Just one? Uhh...okay...umm...

: Is there a reason the main character seems so...closed off? He’s written well, but without any background information at all in the first book, he seems like more of an...afterthought than anything?
: Does he? Because I think he’s plenty interesting even without any of that.
: It takes a very special type of person to groom and manipulate an entire class of underage girls. It takes someone sick. And most people catch their sicknesses from someone else.
: Are you saying...the protagonist is only like this because someone else corrupted him?
: I’m saying you should spend more time thinking about the implications of a character’s actions rather than their motivations for doing so. Unless you want to be bored, that is.
: Any wannabe-psychologist could sit down with a pen and paper and try to tell you about why people act the way they do.
: But with so many of our decisions not based in science or logic but a spontaneous impulse or thought, what matter does motivation carry? If you ask me, none.
: It matters not why someone does the things they do. What matters is what spawns from that. And to me, it’s far more fun to predict the future than to analyze the past.
: T-Thank you, Miss Nagahara! But if you wouldn’t mind-
: Fine, fine. What’s your next question?
: There’s, umm...
: There’s a lot less...girl on girl action in your new book. I just wanted to know if-
: It’s coming. Don’t worry.
: And it’ll be sooner than you think.
scene nodokabooksign11
: Thank you so much! I’m looking forward to reading it!
: Not as much as I’m looking forward to writing it.
: Heheh...heh...
: Hah...
: You know, this is what we get for not reading her book. We could have avoided this.
: Heh...heheh...
: You. In the shirt without sleeves.
scene nodokabooksign12
: Aren’t you the girl who hit on me at the bar on Halloween?
: Hmm...did I do something like that? That doesn’t sound like me. I’m very reclusive.
: No, I’m pretty sure it was you. Also, aren’t you in high school? I’m pretty positive I’ve seen you around the dorms.
: Aren’t you a grown woman? What are you doing hanging out in high school dorms?
: Oh my God! It’s just like the book!
scene nodokabooksign13
: Hey, it’s not that weird! I live there! Of course I’m going to see some girls hanging around!
: Talk about being a fanatic. This woman’s literally trying to become the main character of the book. She’s missing the point entirely.
: I don’t even know this book! I just saw a line and got into it! I do that sometimes!
scene nodokabooksign14
: Why is my mom here?! I barely saw her at all these last couple years and now it’s like I can’t even get away!
: On the bright side...at least she’s not reading Nodoka’s books?
: Mom! Go home!
: Rin! Hey, Rin! Tell everyone how it’s not weird for me to live in the dorms with you!
: It totally is weird! You should leave! I want my life back!
scene nodokabooksign15
: Hey, wait...is that group cosplaying?
: Oh my God! I think they are! That’s almost exactly how I pictured Sensei in the book!
: We have to take his pants off to know for sure...I look kind of like Haruhi, don’t I? Do you think he’ll do it with me? I can pretend I have a husband and everything.
: Oh! And those girls with him must be Ren and Otoka! Do you think they’re his daughters?
: I don’t know, but I suddenly want them to kiss!
: Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss! Kiss!
: I had a feeling something like this might happen...
scene nodokabooksign16
: Now, now. Settle down, everyone. Leave the cosplayers alone.
: I’m sure there are plenty more questions that need to be answered and I don’t have all day...
scene black
The Q&A carries on, getting more and more disturbing with each and every question.
This isn’t just a book.
This is us.
This is our story.
And she’s putting the entire thing on display for everyone...
She’s showing them all who I really am...
She’s showing them everything...
And...
And they...
And they like me...
Why?...
scene nodokabooksign17
: Hey! Bar buddy! Long time, no see. Didn’t realize you read this kind of stuff. That’s not weird or anything. I’m not judging you.
: I don’t read this kind of stuff, Rika. That girl is one of my students.
scene nodokabooksign18
: Okay. That’s a relief because I was totally judging you.
: Haven’t you jerked someone off under the bleachers before? Why are you judging me?
: Dude, that was the 90’s. If you weren’t jerking someone off under the bleachers, what were you even doing?
scene nodokabooksign19
: Also, that’s not even the part I was judging you for. I got laid watching Cannibal Holocaust once. Disturbing content or whatever doesn’t bother me. But super smart people like that?
: That stuff creeps me the fuck out. That girl’s, like...the head of a cult already. And I’m not looking to get sucked into another one of those things.
: Knew there had to be an ulterior motive for her hitting on me. No one wants a single 42 year-old woman covered in tattoos.
: You’re 43! Stop lying to everyone!
scene nodokabooksign20
: No, you stop lying to everyone! I’m going through enough!
: Are you really still in the dorms? It’s been months.
scene nodokabooksign21
: Like I said, I’m going through enough. But things might take a turn for the better soon. We’ll see.
: You got anything planned for the rest of the day? I was gonna go grab dinner if you wanted to tag along.
: I have plans with a cult leader already, but maybe next time.
scene nodokabooksign22

: Suit yourself. You might want to be careful around that girl, though. She denied it, but I totally know she was the one who hit on me. You might be next. Some girls are just into age gaps like that.
: I will remain vigilant and oppose any and all sexual contact with her.
: Cool, cool. Cool.
: I’m gonna give you my phone number.
: You are?
: Yeah. I tried to think of a cool lead-in to that or a way to sound smooth or whatever, but I couldn’t come up with anything. So I’m just gonna give it to you.
: Are you hitting on me right now? Your daughter is like ten feet away.
scene nodokabooksign23
: I’m not hitting on you. I just desperately need friends to distract me from the darkness that is consuming all that I am and Rin keeps telling me I’m 43 and making things even darker.
: Are you sure you’re not hitting on me? Because you can be and I won’t mind.
scene nodokabooksign24
: Aren’t you dating Imani?
: Imani? No. We just work together. Same with Wakana. And I’m pretty sure we told you that.
: Yeah, but my ex told me she loved me and that was clearly a lie, so.
: I’m not dating Imani. And if I was, I probably would have said something about it when the two of you made out.
scene nodokabooksign25
: Ohhhhh...yeah. She was so average that I guess I forgot about it already.
Oh, poor Imani...
I can’t wait to tease her more about this.
scene nodokabooksign26
: Anyway, I’m gonna head out. But you should call me sometime when you’re not busy joining a cult.
: Also, if they try to brand you, don’t let them. It hurts when it happens and then it hurts again when you have to tattoo over it.
: Later.
scene black
$ rikanumber = True
Rika heads out and I return to Rin and Otoha just before our semi-famous author friend rejoins the fray.
Not wanting the crowd to swarm her, the four of us take shelter in the store’s employee lounge for an hour or two as Rin and Otoha give Nodoka a stern lecture on the value of privacy.
I elect to not chime in, despite being perhaps the most violated out of everyone, but it’s not because I’m not upset with her.
In fact, she was right earlier when she said this was something I’d want to see.
I am proud of her — but it’s for all the wrong reasons.
And, disturbed as I may be, I can’t help but feel shocked about how closely she’s watched me.
And just how well she seems to understand.
My curiosity grows stronger, causing several uncertain uncertainties to dissipate.
All the while, she continues to hollow out a segment of my heart to live in.
And I continue to hold my breath so I can feel more of her existence.
It’s the closest I can ever come to feeling one with her.
